subject: Obtaining functional annotations for selected taxa

messages.author: 4ad48a1892b8a420
messages.subject: Obtaining functional annotations for selected taxa
parts:
A number of users have recently requested the ability to obtain functional annotations for selected taxa.
We will provide a matR function to perform this operation in the near future, for now, this procedure should 
enable you to obtain a table of functional annotations for a selected taxa.

I have only used this procedure one time several months ago.  If you use it and run into trouble, please let me know
so I can update this posting accordingly.

Cheers
Kevin


Currently - this is not a use case that we have automated, but there have been several requests for it; this procedure 
will be much simpler in the future. For now, here is the procedure you need to follow in R, using our R package matR.

# (1) Install R - I'd highly recommend installing or upgrading to the most recent version, but anything after 2.15 should work.

# (2) Make sure you have the most recent version of matR (our package for R)
install.packages("devtools", dependencies = TRUE)
library(devtools)
install_github("MG-RAST/matR")
library(matR)
dependencies() 
# (2.b) Install two additional required packages
install.packages("RJSONIO")
install.packages("RCurl")
library(RJSONIO)
library(RCurl)

# (3) If you intend to access private data

# you need to add your MG-RAST key to your matR session

# skip this step if your samples a public

# First you have to get your key from the MG-RAST website

# login here as you normally would

# click on the icon next to your name that looks like a green bust (just left # of the red x to logout. 

# This will take you to your account management page

# Find the section labeled "Preferences" and then click on the button to the

# right of this text "To manage your personal preferences, please click"

# This will open the "Manage Preferences" page. Scroll to the bottom section

# labeled "Web Services" Click on the "generate new key" button, and then

# click on the "set preferences" button just below it.

# The alpha numeric string that appears in the text box is your key

# This key will be valid until the date listed.

# To create a new key just repeat these steps

# Now copy your key, and paste it into a simple text file (Not a word

# document, something like Texedit on a mac or Notepad on a windows PC)

# Let’s say you save the file on your desktop and call it "my_token.txt"

# in R, with matR loaded used this command

msession$setAuth(file="my_token.txt")

# alternatively you can use this command

msession$setAuth()

# hit enter, paste your key when prompted, and then hit enter again

# This key will allow anyone to access your private data -- so be careful with

# it.  For security, the key will be deleted each time you exit R

# For convenience sake I usually keep my key in a file, so I can easily load

# it from file


# (4) Change into the directory with the list
setwd(" \my_documents\")

# (5) load the list of ids into a file
my_ids <- readIDs("my_id_list.txt")
# Note that you can load a list of ids that has one or two columns
# if the file has a single column, matR will assume that it contains the metagenome ids
# if it has two columns, matR will interpret the first column as the id, and the second as a name (any name you 
# want to give it) 

# (6) create a properly formatted list of the sample ids (this will be used in the api call)
api_formatted_id_list <- paste("id=", as.character(my_ids[1]), sep="", collapse="")
for (i in 2:length(my_ids)){ api_formatted_id_list<-(paste(  api_formatted_id_list, "&id=",  as.character(my_ids[2]), sep="", collapse="")) }

# (7) create additional arguments for the api call 
# Since this is not currently a standard operation in matR, you have to construct the API call by specifying several options
result_type=abundance
my_level <- "level3"                                                           # level of the functional annotations that you want to use, valid selections include "level1", "level2", "level3", "function"
my_source <- "Subsystems"                                              # the annotation source that you want to use - valid selections include
my_key <- msession$setAuth(file="~/kevin.matR_key")       # key for your private data (explained above
filter_level = "domain"                                                        # taxonomic level at which you want to filter the data - valid selections include "domain", "phylum", "class", "order", "family", "genus", "species", & "strain"
filter_taxa ="Bacteria"                                                        # single taxa of the indicated level that you want to include (functions for all other taxa will be excluded)
                                                                                        # selecting for multiple taxa is possible - let me know if you need to do this and I will provide an example
# see this page for further details http://api.metagenomics.anl.gov/api.html#matrix

# (8) construct the complete API call
my_call <- paste("http://api.metagenomics.anl.gov/matrix/function?", 
api_formatted_id_list, 
"&result_type=abundance&group_level=", my_level,
"&source=", my_source,
"&hit_type=na&asynchronous=1&auth=", my_key,
"&filter_level=", my_level,
"&filter=", filter_taxa,
collapse="", sep="")

# (9) Perform the call and check the status until it is complete - download the results when it is complete
my_api.call <- fromJSON(getURL(my_call))

check_times = 100    # number of times to check
check_interval = 60   # seconds in between checks -- I'd suggest no more than once a minute


for (i in 1:check_times ){
paste("Checking ", i, " out of ", check_times, "times")
Sys.sleep(check_interval)
my_api.status <- fromJSON(getURL(my_api.call['url']))['status']
  if ( identical( my_api.status, "done" ) ){  }
my_api.data <<- fromJSON(getURL(my_api.call['url']))
}


# note that if your call takes longer than check_times * check_interval you can use this command to check the status at any time
my_api.status <- fromJSON(getURL(my_api.call['url']))['status']

# And this one to download the results when the status is "done"
my_api.data <<- fromJSON(getURL(my_api.call['url']))

# (10) convert downloaded object into a simple R matrix
my_api.matrix <- matrix (unlist (my_api.data$data$data), ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)
my_api.matrix <- as.matrix (Matrix::sparseMatrix (i = 1 + my_api.matrix [,1], j = 1 + my_api.matrix [,2], x = my_api.matrix [,3]))
try (rownames (my_api.matrix) <- sapply (my_api.data$data$rows, `[[`, i = "metadata"))
try (colnames (my_api.matrix) <- sapply (my_api.data$data$columns, `[[`, i = "id"))
# write the table to a tab delimited text file
write.table(my_api.matrix, file = "my_api.matrix.txt", col.names=NA, sep="\t", quote=FALSE)
# convert the table to a matR collection for further analysis with matR 
my_collection <- as(my_api.matrix, "collection")
